# TestOps MCP — Full LLM Reference

> MCP server that connects Claude to Allure TestOps. 148 curated tools + 600+ dynamic OpenAPI endpoints + 2 prompt templates + 4 resources.
> Module: github.com/MimoJanra/TestOpsMCP | Go 1.27+ | Apache 2.0 | MCP protocol 2025-11-25

---

## Architecture

```
cmd/server/main.go          — entry point; --http flag picks transport
internal/
  mcp/
    server.go               — JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatcher, SSE sessions, heartbeat (25s)
    middleware.go           — requestHandler/middlewareFunc, panic recovery, audit chain
    stdio.go                — line-buffered stdin/stdout handler
    protocol.go             — MCP protocol types (version 2025-11-25)
  tools/
    registry.go             — tool/prompt/resource registration, Typed[T] wrapper, per-session token isolation
    prompts.go              — 2 MCP prompt templates (analyze-test-failures, launch-report-summary)
    tools_launches.go       — launch management (14 tools; run/copy/merge are async)
    tools_results.go        — test result actions (6 tools)
    tools_testcases.go      — test case CRUD + run (14 tools)
    tools_testcases_extra.go— metadata, steps, versions, search (30+ tools)
    tools_bulk.go           — bulk operations (22 tools; run/clone are async)
    tools_projects.go       — project management (3 tools)
    tools_analytics.go      — analytics (3 tools)
    tools_relations.go      — test case relations (9 tools)
    tools_customfields.go   — custom field definitions, project attachment, value catalog (13 tools)
    tools_tasks.go          — async task management (3 tools)
    tools_analysis.go       — AI-powered analysis via sampling (1 tool)
    openapi_loader.go       — loads testops.json, builds searchable index
    search_execute.go       — search + execute for 600+ OpenAPI endpoints
    widgets.go              — MCP widget resources; watchLaunch polling
  adapters/allure/
    client.go               — HTTP client, JWT caching, per-session token callback
    models.go               — request/response DTOs
  config/config.go          — env-var loading and validation (users, audit config)
  core/logger.go            — structured logging via log/slog (JSON to stderr), 4 levels
  session/session.go        — context keys: session ID, user, remote addr, ElicitFunc, SamplingFunc
  audit/audit.go            — daily JSONL audit log, configurable retention, auto-cleanup
  tasks/tasks.go            — in-memory async task store (working/succeeded/failed/cancelled)
```

### Transport modes

**Stdio** (default, single user):
- Reads JSON-RPC from stdin, writes to stdout
- Session ID fixed as `"stdio"`
- Max 32 MiB per JSON-RPC line; an oversized line is answered with a JSON-RPC error and the server keeps serving (it used to terminate the server)
- Local file access (`upload_test_case_attachment` `file_path`, `get_test_case_attachment_content` `save_to`) is enabled only in this mode — set from the transport at startup, never from the request
- Used for Claude Desktop local integration

**HTTP + SSE** (multi-user team server):
- `GET /health` — unauthenticated liveness probe, returns `ok`; used by Docker HEALTHCHECK and K8s probes
- `POST /mcp` — streamable HTTP transport (MCP spec 2025-11-25), recommended
- `GET /sse` — legacy SSE stream, returns `session_id` as first event
- `POST /messages?sessionId=<id>` — legacy JSON-RPC request for a session
- Per-session `X-Allure-Token` header stored in Registry
- Named user auth via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (`MCP_AUTH_TOKENS=alice:tok,...`)
- Heartbeat every 25 s, max 64 queued messages per session, 32 MiB max body (fits a 20 MiB attachment as base64)
- Every non-notification request goes through panic recovery + audit middleware
- Elicitation: server sends `elicitation/create` as JSON-RPC *request* (with `id`); client replies with a standard JSON-RPC response `{id, result: {action, content}}`
- Sampling: server sends `sampling/createMessage` requests (with `id`); client replies with standard JSON-RPC response `{id, result: {role, content, stopReason}}`
- Both are dispatched by `handleJSONRPCResponse` keyed on the response `id`; no custom method names required on the client
- Resource subscriptions: `resources/subscribe` / `resources/unsubscribe`; watcher goroutine is tied to session lifetime (`sess.ctx`), not request lifetime; `PublishResource` pushes `notifications/resources/updated` to all subscribed sessions

**Claude Desktop client config (via mcp-remote — required for custom headers):**
Windows:
```json
{"command":"cmd","args":["/c","npx","-y","mcp-remote","https://server/mcp",
  "--header","Authorization:Bearer <token>","--header","X-Allure-Token:<token>"]}
```
macOS/Linux: `"command":"npx","args":["-y","mcp-remote","https://server/mcp",...]`

### Session token isolation

Each HTTP session gets its own Allure API token. Priority:
1. `X-Allure-Token` header on SSE connection → stored in `Registry.sessionTokens[sessID]`
2. `configure_allure_token` tool call → stored per session
3. `ALLURE_TOKEN` env var → global fallback

### JWT caching

`allure.Client` caches JWT tokens keyed by API token string. Auto-refreshes before expiry.

### Async task system

`tasks.Store` runs an in-process background janitor (every 5 min) that deletes succeeded/failed/cancelled tasks older than 1 hour.
`Store.Create(toolName, parentCtx)` uses `context.WithoutCancel(parentCtx)` + 30-minute timeout, so async goroutines carry the originating session ID (for correct token resolution) without being cancelled when the HTTP request ends.
`Store.Run(id, ctx, fn)` wraps `fn` in `recover()` — a panic marks the task Failed instead of crashing the server.

### Completion cache

`Registry.Complete(ctx, refType, promptName, argName, partial)` only calls Allure when `refType == "ref/prompt"`. Results are cached in-process for 30 s (fetched with a 5-second timeout). No upstream calls on every keystroke.

---

## Configuration

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|----------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `ALLURE_BASE_URL` | Yes | — | Allure TestOps URL, e.g. `https://testops.company.com` |
| `ALLURE_TOKEN` | No | — | Global API token (optional for per-user deployments) |
| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` | No | 30 | HTTP timeout seconds (1–600) |
| `PORT` | No | `:3000` | HTTP server port (auto-prefixed with `:` if needed) |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | No | `INFO` | `DEBUG` / `INFO` / `WARN` / `ERROR` |
| `MCP_AUTH_TOKENS` | No | — | Named user tokens: `alice:tok1,bob:tok2` (preferred) |
| `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` | No | — | Single legacy token; treated as user `"default"` |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | No | — (disabled) | CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` value |
| `AUDIT_LOG_PATH` | No | `audit` | Directory for daily audit JSONL files |
| `AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` | No | `30` | Days to keep audit files before auto-deletion |

---

## MCP Protocol Features (2025-11-25)

- **Version negotiation** — server accepts client's requested version if in `["2025-11-25","2025-06-18","2025-03-26","2024-11-05"]`; falls back to latest
- **Pagination** — `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list` return cursor-based pages (50 items). Response includes `nextCursor` when more pages exist. Pass `{"cursor":"50"}` in params to fetch page 2.
- **Completion** — `completion/complete` returns argument suggestions. Supported args: `project_id` (lists real projects), `launch_id` (scans recent launches across first 5 projects)
- **Resource subscriptions** — `resources/subscribe` / `resources/unsubscribe` per URI. Launch dashboard auto-starts a 10 s polling watcher on subscribe.
- **Elicitation** — `elicitation/create` notification → user confirms in UI → `notifications/elicitation/complete`. Applied to `delete_test_case`, `bulk_delete_test_cases`, `remove_test_cases_from_launch` (mode=delete), `delete_launch`, `delete_test_plan` and `delete_defect`.
- **Sampling** — `sampling/createMessage` request → LLM via client → `sampling/createMessage/response`. Used by `analyze_launch_failures`.
- **Capabilities advertised**: `tools`, `resources` (subscribe=true), `prompts`, `logging`, `elicitation`
- **Client capabilities** — the server records the capabilities the client declares in `initialize`; sampling/elicitation requests to a client that didn't declare them fail immediately instead of blocking until timeout
- **Argument validation** — every tool's schema `required` lists (top level and inside array items) are enforced before the handler runs

---

## Tool Reference

### Universal / Meta (3 tools)

#### configure_allure_token
Set or override the Allure API token for the current chat session only.
```json
{
  "token": "string (required) — Allure TestOps API token"
}
```
Returns: `{"status": "configured", "warning": "..."}`

#### search_testops_operations
Search across 600+ OpenAPI-indexed Allure endpoints by intent keyword.
```json
{
  "intent": "string (required) — e.g. 'create project', 'list launches'",
  "limit":  "integer (optional, default 10, max 100)"
}
```
Returns: `{"intent": "...", "results": [...], "total": 600+}`
Each result: `{operation_id, method, path, summary, parameters}`
Matching is token-based (multi-word intents match on their words), verbs hint the HTTP method (e.g. "delete" → DELETE),
v2 paths and exact path segments rank higher, and an exact operation id returns that operation.

#### execute_testops_operation
Execute any endpoint discovered via `search_testops_operations`.
```json
{
  "operation_id": "string (required) — from search results",
  "parameters": {
    "<path_param>": "value",
    "<query_param>": "value",
    "body": "<object or array for request body>"
  }
}
```
Path and query params are matched by name from the spec. Use `"body"` key for array payloads. Large numbers are sent
verbatim (not as `1.78e+12`); an array query param is repeated (`?id=1&id=2`). Binary responses are returned as
`content_base64`.

---

### Launch Management (17 tools)

> **Async operations** — `run_allure_launch`, `copy_launch`, `merge_launches` return `{"task_id": "...", "message": "..."}` immediately and complete in the background. Use `get_task_status` to poll.

#### run_allure_launch
Start a new test launch (async).
```json
{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "launch_name": "string (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"task_id": "abc123", "message": "Launch creation started. Use get_task_status to track progress."}`
Task result on success: `{"launch_id": 123, "status": "started"}`

#### get_launch_status
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"launch_id": N, "status": "OPEN|CLOSED", "closed": bool, "statistic": {"total", "passed", "failed", "broken", "skipped", "unknown"}}`.
The launch DTO has no status field (this used to always return null); a launch is open or closed, and its progress is the per-status result counts.

#### get_launch_report
Get pass/fail statistics for a launch.
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"total": N, "passed": N, "failed": N, "broken": N, "skipped": N, "unknown": N}`

#### list_launches
```json
{
  "project_id": "integer (required)",
  "page": "integer (default 0)",
  "size": "integer (default 10, max 100)"
}
```
Returns paginated list with id, name, status (`OPEN`/`CLOSED`), closed, project_id, created_date, tags. The list endpoint returns no start/end time or environment — use `get_launch_environment` / `get_launch_report`.

#### get_launch_details
Launch metadata: id, name, status (`OPEN`/`CLOSED`), closed, autoclose, external, project_id, created_date, last_modified_date, tags, links, issues, and `statistic` (per-status counts).
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### close_launch
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"status": "closed"}`

#### reopen_launch
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"status": "reopened"}`

#### update_launch
Rename a launch, or toggle autoclose/external. All fields besides launch_id optional.
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)", "name": "string", "autoclose": "boolean", "external": "boolean" }
```
Returns: `{"status": "updated"}`

#### copy_launch
Async. Returns task_id. `launch_name` required by the API even though optional in this tool — defaults to the original launch's name + " (copy)" if omitted. The API responds 202 with no body, so the new launch's ID isn't returned; task result: `{"status": "copied", "message": "..."}` — find the new launch via list_launches.
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)", "launch_name": "string (optional)" }
```

#### merge_launches
Async. Returns task_id. Task result: `{"merged_launch_id": N, "status": "merged"}`. Destructive: the source launches are deleted. Refuses a target that is also a source (a self-merge deleted the launch) and duplicate ids; on partial failure reports which sources were already merged.
```json
{
  "launch_ids": "[integer] (required)",
  "launch_name": "string (required)"
}
```

#### get_launch_environment
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"environment": {"KEY": "VALUE", ...}}`

#### add_test_cases_to_launch
```json
{
  "launch_id": "integer (required)",
  "project_id": "integer (required)",
  "test_case_ids": "[integer] (required)",
  "assignees": "[string] (optional) — usernames"
}
```
Returns: `{"status": "success", "count": N}`

#### add_test_plan_to_launch
```json
{
  "launch_id": "integer (required)",
  "test_plan_id": "integer (required)"
}
```
Returns: `{"status": "success"}`

#### remove_test_cases_from_launch
```json
{
  "launch_id": "integer (required)",
  "test_case_ids": "[integer] (required) — test cases to remove from the launch",
  "mode": "string (hide|delete, default hide)"
}
```
Removes test cases from a launch by resolving each `test_case_id` to its test result(s) in the launch (including retries) and removing them. `mode=hide` excludes them from the report but keeps the data (non-destructive); `mode=delete` permanently deletes the results (no bulk delete API exists, so deletions are issued one-by-one). Returns: `{"launch_id", "mode", "removed_count", "removed_result_ids", "not_found_test_case_ids", "truncated", "failed"?}`.

#### get_launch_defects
```json
{
  "launch_id": "integer (required)",
  "page": "integer (default 0)",
  "size": "integer (default 10, max 100)"
}
```
Returns paginated defect list.

#### get_launch_dashboard
Interactive launch dashboard widget (status, progress bar, pass/fail statistics) rendered inline in Claude Desktop / claude.ai. Only registered when an Allure client is configured.
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### delete_launch
Permanently delete a launch and all its test results. Asks the user to confirm via elicitation.
```json
{ "launch_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"status": "deleted"}`

---

### Test Results (6 tools)

#### list_test_results
```json
{
  "launch_id": "integer (required)",
  "status": "string (optional) — passed|failed|broken|skipped|unknown",
  "page": "integer (default 0)",
  "size": "integer (default 10, max 1000)"
}
```
Returns paginated list: id, name, status, launch_id, start_time, end_time, duration. The API has no server-side
status filter (a "status" query param is silently ignored) — when `status` is set, this scans the launch's results
client-side and paginates over the matches, `page`/`size` applying to the filtered list. The scan is capped at 20,000
results; a `truncated: true` in the response means the cap was hit before the full launch could be scanned.

#### get_test_result
Full result detail including uuid, full_name, description, parameters, tested_by, hidden, manual, category, layer, links.
```json
{ "test_result_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### assign_test_result
```json
{ "test_result_id": "integer (required)", "username": "string (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"status": "assigned"}`. The stored assignee is read back; the tool errors when Allure ignores the assignment (e.g. already resolved results).

#### mute_test_result
```json
{ "test_result_id": "integer (required)", "reason": "string (optional)" }
```
Returns: `{"status": "muted"}`. The mute name column is limited to 255 characters: a longer reason is truncated for the name and kept whole as the reason.

#### resolve_test_result
Mirrors the web UI's "Change status" dialog (Status/Category/Details). Get valid category ids via
`execute_testops_operation` on `GET /api/project/{project_id}/category`.
```json
{
  "test_result_id": "integer (required)",
  "status": "string (required) — failed|broken|passed|skipped|unknown",
  "category_id": "integer (optional)",
  "message": "string (optional) — the \"Details\" field"
}
```
Returns: `{"status": "resolved"}`

#### unmute_test_result
```json
{ "test_result_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"status": "unmuted"}`

---

### Test Cases — Core (11 tools)

#### list_test_cases
```json
{
  "project_id": "integer (required)",
  "page": "integer (default 0)",
  "size": "integer (default 10)"
}
```
Each item includes `automation_status` (`"automated"`/`"manual"`; used to always be null).

#### get_test_case
Full test case: metadata, manual_scenario (steps), tags, members, custom fields, examples, and more.
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### create_test_case
Create a test case, optionally with all its content in one call. Only `project_id` and `name` are required.
`status_id` and `workflow_id` must be passed together. A custom field item sets one value: `value_id` (existing value)
or `name` (found or created by name). Tags given by an unknown name are created. Built-in ids are negative
(e.g. status -1 Draft; custom fields Epic/Feature/Story/Suite -1..-5).
```json
{
  "project_id": "integer (required)",
  "name": "string (required)",
  "description": "string (optional, markdown)",
  "precondition": "string (optional)",
  "expected_result": "string (optional)",
  "full_name": "string (optional)",
  "automated": "boolean (optional, default manual)",
  "status_id": "integer (optional, requires workflow_id)",
  "workflow_id": "integer (optional, requires status_id)",
  "test_layer_id": "integer (optional)",
  "tags": [{"id": N, "name": "..."}],
  "links": [{"name": "...", "type": "...", "url": "... (required)"}],
  "members": [{"id": "N (required, project member id)", "name": "..."}],
  "custom_fields": [{"custom_field_id": "N (required)", "value_id": N, "name": "..."}],
  "steps": [{"body": "string (required)", "expected_result": "string", "steps": ["...sub-steps, same shape"]}]
}
```
Returns the new test case id and `steps_created`.

#### update_test_case
All fields optional except test_case_id; only the fields you pass change. `""` clears a text field and `[]` clears
tags/members/links (both used to be silently ignored); tags, members and links replace the whole list.
`manual_scenario` REPLACES all current steps (including their attachments): the scenario is built through the step
API with real text and expected results (it used to store every body as `<empty>`). `{"steps": []}` removes all steps.
The legacy flat shape `{"steps": [{"type": "body"|"expected", "body": "..."}]}` is still accepted. To change a single
step use `update_test_case_step`.
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "full_name": "string",
  "precondition": "string",
  "expected_result": "string",
  "automated": "boolean",
  "external": "boolean",
  "deleted": "boolean",
  "status_id": "integer",
  "test_layer_id": "integer",
  "workflow_id": "integer",
  "tags": [{"id": N, "name": "..."}],
  "members": [{"id": N, "name": "..."}],
  "links": [{"name": "...", "type": "...", "url": "..."}],
  "manual_scenario": {"steps": [{"body": "string (required)", "expected_result": "string", "steps": ["...sub-steps"]}]}
}
```

#### delete_test_case
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### clone_test_case
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"test_case_id": N, "status": "cloned"}`

#### restore_test_case
Restore a soft-deleted test case.
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### run_test_case
Start a run for a single test case in an existing launch.
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)", "launch_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### search_test_cases
AQL query (per docs.qameta.io/allure-testops/advanced/aql/). Values are case-sensitive (`status = "active"` matches nothing; use `"Active"`) — string literals MUST be double-quoted, not single-quoted; partial match is `~=`, not `~`; custom fields use `cf["Name"] = "value"`. Examples: `name ~= "login"`, `status = "active"`, `tag = "smoke"`, `cf["Priority"] = "Medium"`.
```json
{
  "project_id": "integer (required)",
  "query": "string (required) — AQL/RQL expression",
  "page": "integer (default 0)",
  "size": "integer (default 20)"
}
```

#### suggest_test_cases
Autocomplete / name suggestions.
```json
{
  "project_id": "integer (required)",
  "query": "string (required)",
  "page": "integer (default 0)",
  "size": "integer (default 10)"
}
```

#### validate_test_case_query
Validate AQL/RQL without executing.
```json
{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "query": "string (required)" }
```

---

### Test Cases — Steps & Scenario (10 tools)

#### create_test_case_step
Appended to the end by default. `after_id`/`before_id` insert next to a step; the parent of a nested anchor is
resolved automatically. `expected_result` is the same as a follow-up `update_test_case_step`.
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "body": "string (required) — step text",
  "expected_result": "string (optional)",
  "parent_id": "integer (optional) — nest under this step",
  "after_id": "integer (optional) — insert after this step",
  "before_id": "integer (optional) — insert before this step"
}
```

#### update_test_case_step
Setting `expected_result` always requires `test_case_id` — the API models expected results as a separate linked step (not a plain field on the action step); the tool finds or creates the child entry the web UI actually displays. `test_case_id` is also recommended on a body-only edit so an existing expected result isn't wiped. Setting an expected result keeps the body's rich-text formatting. A file or
table node's body cannot be edited (the API would drop the attachment) — the tool refuses. See [#16](https://github.com/MimoJanra/TestOpsMCP/issues/16) for the underlying tree structure.
```json
{
  "step_id": "integer (required)",
  "test_case_id": "integer (required when setting expected_result; recommended otherwise)",
  "body": "string (optional)",
  "expected_result": "string (optional)"
}
```

#### delete_test_case_step
```json
{ "step_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### move_test_case_step
At least one of `after_id`, `before_id`, `parent_id` is required (without a position the API silently un-nested the
step). Pass `test_case_id` with `after_id`/`before_id` so the anchor's parent is resolved — the API 404s on a nested
anchor without it. To move a sub-step to the top level, anchor it to a top-level step.
```json
{
  "step_id": "integer (required)",
  "test_case_id": "integer (recommended) — resolves the anchor's parent",
  "after_id": "integer (optional) — place after this step",
  "before_id": "integer (optional) — place before this step",
  "parent_id": "integer (optional) — new parent; alone it appends to that parent"
}
```

#### copy_test_case_step
Duplicates a step with its sub-steps, expected result and attachments. Returns the copy's `step_id` when
`test_case_id` is given.
```json
{
  "step_id": "integer (required)",
  "test_case_id": "integer (recommended) — resolves the anchor's parent, returns the new step_id",
  "after_id": "integer (optional)",
  "before_id": "integer (optional)",
  "parent_id": "integer (optional)"
}
```

#### delete_test_case_scenario
Delete all steps from a test case.
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### get_test_case_scenario_from_run
Get steps captured from the last automated run.
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### detach_test_case_automation
Convert automated test case back to manual. Omitted `status_id`/`workflow_id` keep the current ones (they used to be
sent as 0, which failed).
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "status_id": "integer (optional; built-in ids are negative, e.g. -1 Draft)",
  "workflow_id": "integer (optional)",
  "use_scenario_from_test_result": "boolean (optional) — copy the latest automated run's steps into the manual scenario"
}
```

#### get_test_case_steps
Normalized step list including every step's ID (needed for move/copy/delete_test_case_step). An empty
`scenarioSteps` with `hasManualScenario: false` on `get_test_case` means the content may live in the legacy
`scenario` field.
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### get_test_case_scenario
Readable scenario: ordered steps with names, keywords, expected results and nesting (same data as `get_test_case_steps`).
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

---

### Test Cases — Metadata (15 tools)

#### get_test_case_tags / set_test_case_tags
get: `{ "test_case_id": integer }`
set (full replace):
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "tags": [{"id": N, "name": "..."}]  // pass complete desired list; [] removes all
}
```
A tag needs either `id` (existing) or `name` — a name that doesn't exist yet creates the tag (no 409; tags are global, not per project).

#### create_test_tag
Creates a new project-wide tag by name and returns its id. Use when you need a tag that doesn't exist yet, then attach the returned id via `set_test_case_tags` or `bulk_add_test_case_tags`.
```json
{ "name": "string (required)" }
```
→ `{ "id": N, "name": "..." }`

#### get_test_case_issues / set_test_case_issues
get: `{ "test_case_id": integer }` → each issue has `id`, `display_name` (the issue key; used to always be empty), `url`,
`integration_id`, `closed`, `summary`, `status`.
set (full replace; `integration_id` and `display_name` are required per issue — the key is sent to the API as `name`,
without which every call 500'd):
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "issues": [{
    "id": N,
    "display_name": "PROJ-123 (required)",
    "url": "https://...",
    "integration_id": "N (required)",
    "closed": false
  }]
}
```

#### get_test_case_examples / set_test_case_examples
get: `{ "test_case_id": integer }` → all rows (used to be capped at 10)
set (parametrized data table):
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "examples": [
    [{"name": "username", "value": "admin"}, {"name": "password", "value": "secret"}]
  ]
}
```

#### get_test_case_custom_fields / update_test_case_custom_fields
get: `{ "test_case_id": integer }`
update: each value needs BOTH `id` and `name` — an id-only value is rejected with a not-null constraint on the value's name. Get both via `list_custom_field_values` or `get_test_case_custom_fields`.
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "custom_fields": [{"custom_field_id": N, "values": [{"id": N, "name": "..."}]}]
}
```

#### list_custom_field_values
Lists the valid values defined for a custom field within a project (e.g. allowed Priority/Section options), so you can pick a real value ID instead of guessing. Get `custom_field_id` from `get_test_case_custom_fields` on any test case in the project.
```json
{
  "project_id": "integer (required)",
  "custom_field_id": "integer (required)",
  "query": "string (optional, filter by value name)",
  "page": "integer (optional, default 0)",
  "size": "integer (optional, default 10)"
}
```

#### get_test_case_keys / set_test_case_keys
get: `{ "test_case_id": integer }`
set (Jira/Azure keys, full replace; each key needs `integration_id` and `name` — the API silently drops a key without them, so the tool refuses it):
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "keys": [{"id": N, "integration_id": N, "name": "TC-1", "url": "https://..."}]
}
```

#### get_test_case_relations / set_test_case_relations
get: `{ "test_case_id": integer }`
set (full replace — pass the complete list you want to keep). `type` is required, one of:
`related to`, `clones`, `is cloned by`, `duplicates`, `is duplicated by`, `automates`, `is automated by`:
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "relations": [{"target_id": N, "target_name": "...", "type": "clones"}]
}
```

#### get_test_case_workflow
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

---

### Custom Fields — Definitions, Project Attachment & Values (13 tools)

Three layers: a custom field **definition** (org-wide, e.g. "Priority"), its **project attachment** (a project opts in, and sets required/locked/default there), and its **value catalog** within a project (the selectable options, e.g. "High"/"Low"). Setting values *on a test case* is `update_test_case_custom_fields` (above) — these tools manage the fields and their options, not test-case assignments.

#### create_custom_field / get_custom_field / update_custom_field / delete_custom_field
create: `{ "name": "string (required)", "required": "boolean (required)", "single_select": "boolean (optional)" }`
get/delete: `{ "custom_field_id": integer }`
update (all fields optional, only passed ones change):
```json
{
  "custom_field_id": "integer (required)",
  "name": "string (optional)",
  "required": "boolean (optional)",
  "single_select": "boolean (optional)",
  "locked": "boolean (optional)"
}
```
`delete_custom_field` is permanent — prefer `set_custom_field_archived` for a reversible removal. `locked` does not block
edits through the API. Built-in fields have negative ids (Epic/Feature/Story/Suite/Component) and are accepted by
`get_custom_field`, `get/update_project_custom_field`, `create_custom_field_value` and `list_custom_field_values`.

#### set_custom_field_archived
```json
{ "custom_field_id": "integer (required)", "archived": "boolean (required)" }
```

#### list_project_custom_fields / get_project_custom_field
list: `{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "query": "string (optional)", "page": "integer (optional, default 0)", "size": "integer (optional, default 10)" }`
get one: `{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "custom_field_id": "integer (required)" }` → project-scoped required/locked/default settings plus the field definition. A field not attached to the project returns a clear error (used to be "decode response: EOF").

#### add_custom_fields_to_project / remove_custom_field_from_project
add: `{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "custom_field_ids": [N, ...] }` → reports ids that were not attached (the API silently ignores unknown ids)
remove: `{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "custom_field_id": "integer (required)" }` (detaches only — doesn't delete the field definition or its values)

#### update_project_custom_field
The current replacement for the API's deprecated set-required/set-default endpoints. All fields optional, only passed ones change:
```json
{
  "project_id": "integer (required)",
  "custom_field_id": "integer (required)",
  "required": "boolean (optional)",
  "locked": "boolean (optional)",
  "default_custom_field_value_id": "integer (optional)"
}
```

#### create_custom_field_value / update_custom_field_value / delete_custom_field_value
create: `{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "custom_field_id": "integer (required)", "name": "string (required)", "default": "boolean (optional)" }`
update (all fields optional, only passed ones change): `{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "value_id": "integer (required)", "name": "string (optional)", "default": "boolean (optional)", "global": "boolean (optional)" }`
delete: `{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "value_id": "integer (required)" }` — test cases currently set to this value lose it.
Renaming a value gives it a new id; test cases follow. `global: true` is irreversible.

---

### Test Cases — Members & Links (6 tools)

#### get_test_case_members
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns each member's id, name and `role`.

#### add_test_case_members
Additive: existing members are kept (v2 bulk member/add; this used to replace all members). `role` is optional — the
project's role scheme decides the stored role. The member `id` must be an existing collaborator on the test case's
project (an org-wide user id fails with "Some role users not found") — find one via `execute_testops_operation` on
`GET /api/member/suggest?projectId=`.
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "members": [{"id": "N (required)", "name": "...", "role": {"id": -1, "name": "Owner"}}]
}
```

#### remove_test_case_members
`project_id` is optional (looked up from the test case); a `project_id` that doesn't match the test case's project is
refused (it used to be a silent no-op).
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "member_ids": [N, N],
  "project_id": "integer (optional)"
}
```

#### get_test_case_external_links
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### add_test_case_external_link
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "name": "string (optional)",
  "type": "string (optional)",
  "url": "string (required)"
}
```

#### delete_test_case_external_link
```json
{ "link_id": "integer (required)" }
```

### Test Cases — Defects (3 tools)

#### get_test_case_defects
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### add_test_case_defect
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "display_name": "string — bug tracker issue key (required)",
  "url": "string (optional)",
  "integration_id": "integer (required)"
}
```

#### remove_test_case_defect
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)", "defect_id": "integer (required)" }
```

### Defects (5 tools)

Project-level defects. Link one to a test case with `add_test_case_defect`. `delete_defect` asks the user to confirm.

#### list_defects
Newest first.
```json
{
  "project_id": "integer (required)",
  "name_filter": "string (optional) — name substring",
  "status": "string (optional) — open|closed",
  "page": "integer (default 0)",
  "size": "integer (default 20, max 100)"
}
```
Returns `{"defects": [{id, name, closed, created_date}], "page", "total", "is_last"}`.

#### get_defect
```json
{ "defect_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns name, description, open/closed state and linked `issue` (`id`, `key`, `url`) when present.

#### create_defect
```json
{ "project_id": "integer (required)", "name": "string (required)", "description": "string (optional)" }
```
Returns `{"id", "name", "project_id"}`.

#### update_defect
Only the fields you pass change; `closed: true` closes, `false` reopens.
```json
{ "defect_id": "integer (required)", "name": "string (optional)", "description": "string (optional)", "closed": "boolean (optional)" }
```

#### delete_defect
Permanent; test cases and results only lose the link. Prefer `update_defect` with `closed: true`.
```json
{ "defect_id": "integer (required)" }
```

### Test Cases — Versions & Attachments (10 tools)

#### list_test_case_versions
```json
{ "test_case_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### create_test_case_version
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "title": "string (required)",
  "description": "string (optional)"
}
```

#### restore_test_case_version
```json
{ "version_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### get_test_case_version_data
```json
{ "version_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### delete_test_case_version
```json
{ "version_id": "integer (required)" }
```

#### get_test_case_attachments
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "integer (required)",
  "page": "integer (default 0)",
  "size": "integer (default 20)"
}
```
Each attachment: `id`, `name`, `content_type`, `size` (real content length), `missed`.

#### get_test_case_attachment_content
Download an attachment. Text content (text/*, JSON, CSV, XML) is returned as `content`, anything else as
`content_base64`. `save_to` writes the file to disk instead — local stdio mode only, and the file must not exist yet
(never overwrites). Max 20 MiB.
```json
{ "attachment_id": "integer (required)", "save_to": "string (optional, stdio only)" }
```
Returns `attachment_id`, `content_type`, `size`, and `content` / `content_base64` / `saved_to`.

#### upload_test_case_attachment
Upload a file to a test case; with `step_id` also show it in that step (the step's "File" block in the web UI —
a child scenario node holding the attachment). `target`: `step` (default) or `expected_result` (the step must already
have an expected result). `file_path` works only in local stdio mode — on a shared HTTP server it would read the
server's disk, so pass `content_base64` + `file_name` there. Max 20 MiB (the base64 form must fit in one 32 MiB MCP message). No v2 endpoint exists for this upload.
```json
{"test_case_id": "integer (required)", "file_path": "string", "content_base64": "string", "file_name": "string", "content_type": "string (optional, guessed)", "step_id": "integer (optional)", "target": "step|expected_result"}
```
Returns `attachment_id`, `name`, `content_type`, `content_length`, and `node_id` when attached to a step.

#### add_test_case_step_table
Add a table to a step (the step's "Table" block). In Allure a step table is a CSV attachment shown in the step, so
this uploads `rows` as `text/csv` and attaches it.
```json
{"test_case_id": "integer (required)", "step_id": "integer (required)", "rows": "[[string]] (required)", "name": "string (default \"Table\")", "target": "step|expected_result"}
```

#### delete_test_case_attachment
```json
{ "attachment_id": "integer (required)" }
```

### Test Cases — Folder Tree (7 tools)

In Allure a "folder" is a value of a custom field, and it only exists within a named **tree** built from custom
fields (e.g. the "Suites" tree groups by the Suite field; "Features" by Feature → Story). Every folder tool takes a
`tree_id` (optional when the project has exactly one tree) and addresses positions by **node id**, not by path.
All of these use the v2 tree API; the v1 path-based endpoints failed ("tree has no group at level 0").

#### list_test_case_trees
```json
{"project_id": "integer (required)"}
```
Returns `{"trees": [{"id": 353, "name": "Suites"}, ...]}`.

#### browse_test_case_tree
One level of a tree: folders and test cases directly inside `parent_node_id` (tree root when omitted).
```json
{"project_id": "integer (required)", "tree_id": "integer (optional)", "parent_node_id": "integer (optional)", "page": "integer (default 0)", "size": "integer (default 50)"}
```
Returns `tree_id`, `node_id`, `folders: [{id, name, test_case_count, custom_field_value_id}]`, `test_cases: [{test_case_id, leaf_id, name, status}]`, `total`.
Listing is sorted with tiebreakers (name, createdDate, testCaseId) so paging doesn't duplicate or skip same-named items.

#### get_test_case_tree_folders
Same parameters as browse_test_case_tree, folders only. `page`/`size` apply to the folder list: the tool collects all
folders of the level first (the API interleaves folders with test cases, so pages used to come back empty). Returns `total`.

#### move_test_cases_to_folder
Move test cases into folder `node_id` (tree root when omitted) — sets the test case's custom field value for that
folder. Asynchronous. The API takes tree leaf ids, which change on every move; the tool resolves them from the test
case ids right before moving. Test cases not present in the tree come back in `not_found_test_case_ids`. `node_id`
must be a folder of the tree — a leaf id, unknown id or another tree's folder is refused (it used to silently strip
the test cases' folders).
```json
{"project_id": "integer (required)", "tree_id": "integer (optional)", "test_case_ids": "[integer] (required)", "node_id": "integer (optional)"}
```

#### create_test_case_folder
Create a folder under `parent_node_id` (tree root when omitted). Returns `folder_id` (use it as `node_id` /
`parent_node_id`) and the underlying `custom_field_value_id`.
```json
{"project_id": "integer (required)", "tree_id": "integer (optional)", "name": "string (required)", "parent_node_id": "integer (optional)"}
```
`parent_node_id` is validated the same way as `move_test_cases_to_folder`'s `node_id`.

#### rename_test_case_folder
Rename a folder in place: it keeps its node id and its test cases follow. Same-named folders elsewhere in the tree are
not affected.
```json
{"project_id": "integer (required)", "tree_id": "integer (optional)", "node_id": "integer (required)", "name": "string (required)"}
```
Returns `{"status": "renamed", "node_id", "tree_id"}`.

#### delete_test_case_folder
Delete a folder. Its test cases are not deleted — they lose this folder assignment. Also removes the folder's backing
custom field value unless another (same-named) folder shares it; then the folder stays empty and `status` is
`"emptied"` with a `warning`. Do not use `delete_custom_field_value` for this: one value can back several folders.
```json
{"project_id": "integer (required)", "tree_id": "integer (optional)", "node_id": "integer (required)"}
```
Returns `{"status": "deleted"|"emptied", "node_id", "tree_id", "warning"?}`.

---

### Bulk Test Case Operations (15 tools)

All bulk test case tools accept `project_id` (integer, required) and `test_case_ids` ([integer], required).

#### bulk_set_test_case_status
```json
{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "status_id": N, "workflow_id": N }
```

#### bulk_add_test_case_tags / bulk_remove_test_case_tags
```json
{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "tags": [{"id": N, "name": "..."}] }
```

#### bulk_clone_test_cases
Async (background task). The API clones asynchronously (202, no body) and does not return the new ids — find the
clones with `list_test_cases`/`search_test_cases`; a `name_suffix` makes them easy to spot. Status resets to Draft.
```json
{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "name_suffix": "string (optional)", "ignore_tags": "boolean (optional)" }
```

#### bulk_mute_test_cases
```json
{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "reason": "string (optional, defaults to \"Muted via MCP\")" }
```
A reason over 255 characters is truncated for the mute name and kept whole as the reason.

#### bulk_delete_test_cases
```json
{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...] }
```

#### bulk_move_test_cases
```json
{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "to_project_id": N }
```

#### bulk_set_test_case_layer
```json
{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "layer_id": N }
```

#### bulk_add_test_case_members / bulk_remove_test_case_members
add: each member needs a `role` (API 400s with a misleading "Some role users not found" if omitted — get valid role
ids via `execute_testops_operation` on `GET /api/role`, e.g. `-1` "Owner"); `id` must be an existing project
collaborator (via `GET /api/member/suggest?projectId=`), not just any org-wide user id —
`{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "members": [{"id": N, "name": "...", "role": {"id": -1, "name": "Owner"}}] }`
remove: `{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "member_ids": [N] }`

#### bulk_add_test_case_custom_fields / bulk_remove_test_case_custom_fields
add: each value needs BOTH `id` and `name` (an id-only value is rejected with a not-null constraint on the value's name) — `{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "custom_fields": [{"custom_field_id": N, "values": [{"id": N, "name": "..."}]}] }`
remove: `{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "custom_field_ids": [N] }`

#### bulk_add_test_case_external_links
```json
{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "links": [{"name": "...", "type": "...", "url": "..."}] }
```

#### bulk_add_test_case_issues / bulk_remove_test_case_issues
add: `integration_id` and `display_name` are required per issue (an issue without them links every issue in the
instance, so the tool refuses it) — `{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "issues": [{"id": N, "display_name": "PROJ-1", "url": "...", "integration_id": N}] }`
remove: `{ "project_id": N, "test_case_ids": [...], "issue_ids": [N] }`

### Bulk Test Result Operations (4 tools)

All accept `launch_id` (integer, required) and `test_result_ids` ([integer], required).

#### bulk_assign_test_results
Several assignees are distributed round-robin; omitting assignees unassigns. Not-run results are skipped.
```json
{ "launch_id": N, "test_result_ids": [...], "assignees": ["username1"] }
```

#### bulk_mute_test_results
A reason over 255 characters is truncated for the mute name and kept whole as the reason.
```json
{ "launch_id": N, "test_result_ids": [...], "reason": "string (optional)" }
```

#### bulk_unmute_test_results
Also removes the test cases' mute records, so they leave the project's muted list.
```json
{ "launch_id": N, "test_result_ids": [...] }
```

#### bulk_resolve_test_results
Mirrors the web UI's "Change status" dialog (Status/Category/Details), applied to many results at once.
```json
{ "launch_id": N, "test_result_ids": [...], "status": "string (required)", "category_id": "integer (optional)", "message": "string (optional)" }
```

### Projects (4 tools)

#### list_projects
```json
{ "page": "integer (default 0)", "size": "integer (default 10, max 100)" }
```
Returns: `{"projects": [{"id": N, "name": "...", "code": "..."}], "page", "size", "total", "is_last"}`. `code` is the
project abbreviation (API field `abbr`; it used to always be empty).

#### find_project
```json
{ "query": "string (required, name or code, case-insensitive substring)", "limit": "integer (default 20, max 100)" }
```
Resolves a human-readable project name/code (e.g. `TSi`) to its numeric ID by scanning `/api/project` client-side (no server-side name filter exists). Returns: `{"query", "matches": [{"id": N, "name": "...", "code": "..."}], "count", "scanned", "truncated"}`.

#### get_project
```json
{ "project_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns: id, name, code, description.

#### get_project_stats
```json
{ "project_id": "integer (required)" }
```
Returns test count, run statistics.

## OpenAPI Fallback (search + execute)

If a tool doesn't cover a needed endpoint, use the two-step fallback:

```
1. search_testops_operations(intent="your goal")
   → returns list of {operation_id, method, path, summary, parameters}

2. execute_testops_operation(operation_id="...", parameters={...})
   → executes the endpoint, returns parsed JSON
```

The index covers all endpoints from `testops.json` in the project root. The search uses fuzzy keyword matching on operation ID, tags, summary, description, and path.

For array request bodies: `parameters: {"body": [item1, item2]}`
For mixed path+body: `parameters: {"id": 123, "body": {...}}`

---

## Common Patterns

### Start a test run and wait for completion
```
run_allure_launch(project_id=1, launch_name="Smoke CI #42")
→ {launch_id: 999}

get_launch_status(launch_id=999)   # poll until status != RUNNING
→ {status: "DONE"}

get_launch_report(launch_id=999)
→ {total: 156, passed: 142, failed: 10, broken: 4}
```

### Investigate failures
```
list_test_results(launch_id=999, status="FAILED", size=20)
→ [{id: 5001, name: "Auth login test", ...}, ...]

get_test_result(test_result_id=5001)
→ full detail with description, parameters, steps
```

### Bulk update test cases from a query
```
search_test_cases(project_id=1, query="tag = 'flaky'")
→ [{id: 101}, {id: 102}, ...]

bulk_add_test_case_tags(project_id=1, test_case_ids=[101,102], tags=[{name:"needs-fix"}])
```

### Create and version a test case
```
create_test_case(project_id=1, name="Login with MFA")
→ {test_case_id: 200}

create_test_case_step(test_case_id=200, name="Navigate to login page")
create_test_case_step(test_case_id=200, name="Enter credentials")
create_test_case_step(test_case_id=200, name="Verify MFA prompt")

create_test_case_version(test_case_id=200, title="v1.0 — initial")
```

---

### Async Task Management (3 tools)

Long-running operations (run_allure_launch, copy_launch, merge_launches, bulk_run_*, bulk_clone_test_cases) return `{"task_id": "...", "message": "..."}` immediately and run in the background.

#### get_task_status
```json
{ "task_id": "string (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"id": "...", "tool": "run_allure_launch", "status": "working|succeeded|failed|cancelled", "result": {...}, "error": "...", "created_at": "...", "updated_at": "..."}`

#### list_running_tasks
No parameters. Returns: `{"tasks": [...], "count": N}` — only tasks with status=working.

#### cancel_task
```json
{ "task_id": "string (required)" }
```
Returns: `{"status": "cancelled", "task_id": "..."}` — signals the background goroutine via context cancellation. A
cancelled task stays cancelled; if the work finishes later, its outcome is reported in the task's message.

---

### AI Analysis (1 tool)

#### analyze_launch_failures
Fetches failed test results from a launch and uses MCP sampling (asks Claude via the client) to identify root causes and suggest fixes. Returns a plain-text analysis.

**Requires:** client that supports `sampling/createMessage`.
```json
{
  "launch_id": "integer (required)",
  "max_failures": "integer (optional, default 20, max 50)"
}
```
Returns: `{"launch_id": N, "failures": N, "analysis": "...<Claude's analysis>..."}`. Analyzes failed and broken results;
errors on a nonexistent launch.
If sampling unavailable: returns `summary` of raw failures with `error` field.

---

## Pagination Convention

All list/search tools use 0-based page numbers. Response always includes:
- `page` — current page number
- `size` — items per page
- `total` — total item count
- `is_last` — boolean, true when no more pages

Default page size: 10. Max: 100 (enforced server-side).

---

## Error Handling

Tools return errors as MCP error responses. Common causes:
- `project_id must be positive` — invalid ID
- `token cannot be empty` — configure_allure_token called with blank token
- `operations index not available` — testops.json not found in project root
- `operation not found: <id>` — invalid operation_id in execute
- HTTP errors from Allure API are wrapped: `get launch status: 404 Not Found`

---

## Security Notes

- Never log API tokens (masked in logs)
- `configure_allure_token` warns users: token is session-only, not persisted
- HTTP mode: configure `MCP_AUTH_TOKENS` with per-user named tokens in production
- Audit log records every request: user, session, remote addr, method, tool, status, duration
- Use HTTPS in production (nginx/Caddy reverse proxy)
- Set `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` to specific origin (not `*`) in production
- Request bodies are capped at 32 MiB; a reverse proxy must allow that much (`client_max_body_size 32m`) for attachment uploads
- `file_path` (upload) and `save_to` (download) are stdio-only; `save_to` never overwrites an existing file (O_EXCL)

---

## Build & Run

```bash
# Build
go build -o testops-mcp ./cmd/server

# Stdio mode (Claude Desktop)
./testops-mcp

# HTTP mode (team server)
./testops-mcp --http

# Docker
docker pull ghcr.io/MimoJanra/TestOpsMCP:latest
docker run -e ALLURE_BASE_URL=https://testops.company.com \
           -e ALLURE_TOKEN=mytoken \
           -p 3000:3000 \
           ghcr.io/MimoJanra/TestOpsMCP:latest --http
```

---

## MCP Prompts

Server advertises `prompts` capability. Clients call `prompts/list` then `prompts/get` with argument values.

### analyze-test-failures
Analyze failed, broken, and skipped tests in an Allure launch to identify patterns and root causes.

Arguments:
- `launch_id` (required) — Allure launch ID
- `project_id` (optional) — Allure project ID for additional context

Generated user message: instructs Claude to get launch details, list failures, group by error pattern, surface critical issues.

### launch-report-summary
Generate a concise executive summary for an Allure TestOps launch.

Arguments:
- `launch_id` (required) — Allure launch ID
- `project_id` (optional) — Allure project ID

Generated user message: instructs Claude to retrieve stats and report pass rate, counts, duration, environment, and top 3 failures.

---

## MCP Resources

Server advertises `resources` capability. Clients call `resources/list` then `resources/read` with the URI.

| URI | MIME type | Description |
|-----|-----------|-------------|
| `allure://docs/quickstart` | `text/markdown` | Static quickstart listing tool groups, prompts, and setup instructions. Always available. |
| `ui://widgets/launch-dashboard` | `text/html;profile=mcp-app` | Interactive launch dashboard with progress bar and stats (requires Allure token). |
| `ui://widgets/action-picker` | `text/html;profile=mcp-app` | Search/filter picker for 600+ OpenAPI operations. |
| `ui://widgets/results-display` | `text/html;profile=mcp-app` | JSON result viewer for `execute_testops_operation` output. |

Widget resources embed the `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` browser bundle (fetched from CDN on first use; falls back to a minimal stub if unavailable).
